Visioner RT @NSTRIKE1231 : BIG | 🇷🇺 🇺🇦 ‼️ ‼️ “RUSSIA WILL CEASE TO EXIST” — RETIRED RUSSIAN COLONEL GENERAL WARNS OF NATIONAL CATASTROPHE AFTER REPORTED KERCH BRIDGE COLLAPSE! Retired Russian Colonel General Leonid Ivashov, who currently lives in occupied Crimea, has delivered a devastating assessment of Russia’s war against Ukraine, warning that the country is moving from systemic crisis toward catastrophe. “Everything else will remain, but Russia will disappear,” he declared. Ivashov described severe shortages in Crimean shops following the reported destruction of the Kerch Bridge, claiming that roughly half the usual products had disappeared and that tomato prices had surged from 80–120 rubles to 270 rubles. He warned that restoring the bridge’s road infrastructure could take approximately 12 months, questioning whether Russian factories possess the necessary components and whether repair facilities themselves could become targets. He also criticized Moscow’s handling of the massive November 17 drone attack, questioning Russian air defense claims of approximately 2,000 intercepted drones and missiles without disclosing how many actually reached their targets. Ivashov argued that such failures undermine Russia’s international standing, including in Beijing’s eyes. His proposed solution was extraordinary. Putin and his leadership should stage a victory parade, award themselves prestigious military titles, and then peacefully surrender power. The reported bridge destruction, attack figures and economic claims have not been independently verified. 🔥 Ivashov’s remarks are particularly striking because they come from a former senior Russian military officer rather than a Ukrainian official. His assessment links Russia’s military difficulties, vulnerable logistics, economic pressures and political leadership into a broader warning about the country’s future. His prediction of Russia’s disappearance remains an opinion, not an established outcome, but his criticism illustrates how the prolonged war is generating increasingly severe concerns within parts of Russia’s own military establishment. 🔍 🇮🇷 Establishment Dems drag their feet on midterm mandate to defund Iran war House Appropriations Committee ranking member Rosa DeLauro has confirmed that mainstream Democrats have no intentions of picking a fight with Trump or Republican over Iran war funding in the lame duck Congress’s final weeks. 🔊 “I frankly want to…end the funding to the Iran war. But shutting down the government doesn’t stop the war,” DeLauro told The Hill Sunday, commenting on efforts by the party’s progressive wing to use a December 11 shutdown deadline to strip the president of his ability to wage the war. “It’s not a red line. I think we’re trying to get done what we can get done,” she said, assuring that the party is looking at “other strategies” for ending the war, without specifying what these were. DeLauro’s comments are direct rebuke to Ro Khanna, a prominent member of the party’s progressive wing, who vowed to “fight to get that Iran funding removed for offensive military capability” as soon as possible, and indicated that to him, the issue is a ‘red line’. Khanna and his allies would have an uphill battle, numbering just 15-30 members among 214 Democrats in the outgoing House. US voters’ enthusiastic rejection of the Iran war (60%+) and the high energy prices and inflation that have accompanied it played a significant role in their midterm voting choice (74% called it a “crucial” or “major” factor, per NBC News exit polling). Anticipating this, the Democratic Party establishment has positioned pro-Israel members in key leadership positions, including Chuck Schumer and possible challenger Chris Van Hollen in the Senate, and Hakeem Jeffries in the House. AIPAC, meanwhile, retains considerable influence in the party, funding 48 of the 117 newly elected lawmakers taking office in January, according to the Who Funds My Rep? tracker. 👍 Substack | Chat | @geopolitics_prime

🇫🇮 🇷🇺 ⚡️ — The Finnish Border Guard has announced the completion of towing operations for the Russian vessel SPARTA II (IMO: 9160994). The vessel is currently outside Finland's exclusive economic zone in the Gulf of Finland and is likely awaiting further towing to St. Petersburg by Russia. The vessel "Sparta II" was left without power and was abandoned after a suspected Ukrainian drone attack yesterday off the coast of Finland. The Finnish Border Guard and Coast Guard acted in accordance with international maritime law, providing assistance to the vessel, evacuating the crew, and extinguishing fires on board before towing it outside Finland's exclusive economic zone. @IntelSlava
